close_reason: Landed in commit 5a11ac0. TasksBackend::compute_task_utc_times renamed to compute_utc_times, args (caller, account_id) added, return type changed sync tuple → impl Future + Send. Regression test compute_utc_times_receives_validated_account_id added. cargo fmt / clippy --workspace -D warnings / test --workspace / doc -D warnings all green. The naming alignment opportunity mentioned in the bead body was taken (calendars-canonical name).
description:
**Divergence**: same semantic ('project local time + tz hint into UTC, return (start, end)-or-(None, None)'), two different argument sets.

- CalendarsBackend::compute_utc_times (crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:445):
    fn compute_utc_times(&self, caller: &Self::CallerCtx, account_id: &Id, event: &CalendarEvent, tz_hint: Option<&str>) -> Result<(Option<UTCDate>, Option<UTCDate>), ...>
- TasksBackend::compute_task_utc_times (crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/backend.rs:325):
    fn compute_task_utc_times(&self, task: &Task, tz_hint: Option<&str>) -> Result<(Option<UTCDate>, Option<UTCDate>), ...>

**Caller-observable effect**: a backend that wants to vary UTC computation per caller — e.g. resolve a per-user default tz when `tz_hint` is `None` from the calling user's preferences, not from a global default — works in calendars and is structurally impossible in tasks without a trait-shape break. This is workspace AGENTS.md 'Backend caps and limits' policy applied to a non-caps method: plumb `caller, account_id` even when the default ignores them.

**Outlier**: tasks-server. Calendars-server is the more future-proof shape and is consistent with the workspace policy precedent (caller/account threaded into every method that *might* one day need to vary per caller, even if the reference impl ignores them).

**Fix**: extend `TasksBackend::compute_task_utc_times` signature to take `caller: &Self::CallerCtx, account_id: &Id` in front, like the calendars version. Default impl can still ignore them (`let _ = (caller, account_id);`). Breaking change to TasksBackend trait; pre-1.0 so acceptable. The handler call site in tasks-server passes them already (the dispatcher has them).

**Naming alignment opportunity**: the calendars version is `compute_utc_times` (no spec-object prefix); the tasks version is `compute_task_utc_times` (with prefix). Since the methods live on object-specific traits (`CalendarsBackend`, `TasksBackend`), the prefix is redundant. Calendars's name is canonical. Either rename tasks to `compute_utc_times` (also breaking) or document the prefix as an intentional convention. Same change touches both consistency axes.
title: calendars-server / tasks-server: compute_utc_times signature divergence (calendars takes caller/account; tasks does not)
